name: PreserveTube
description: PreserveTube is a time capsule for YouTube videos! It allows you to preserve any YouTube video, creating a snapshot that will always be available even if the original video disappears or is taken down.
author: Freeb

captcha.userAgent: Mozilla/5.0 (Linux; Android 14) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/131.0.6778.200 Mobile Safari/537.36

settings.name: Enable YouTube Channel Separation
settings.description: When enabled, YouTube channel URLs will be treated as PreserveTube channels with separated IDs (prefixed with 'preservetube://') to avoid conflicts with the YouTube plugin. Disable to keep YouTube channel URLs pointing to the YouTube plugin instead.

settings.name: Enable Archiving to PreserveTube
settings.description: When enabled, unarchived YouTube videos will prompt you to archive them on PreserveTube via captcha. Disabled by default so unarchived videos open in the YouTube plugin instead.
settings.warningDialog: By enabling this, you agree to only use this feature for videos that you genuinely believe should be preserved long term.

5: Rewrote getContentDetails to scrape HTML instead of blocked JSON API
Added YouTube channel separation setting with ID prefixing
Added archiving toggle (off by default) with warning dialog
Fixed channel avatar parsing from yt3.googleusercontent.com
Rewrote parseVideoCardsFromHtml with proper depth counting
7: Fixed channel name and thumbnail lookup by reading the channel profile from a video watch page (channel pages are now Cloudflare challenged and no longer contain the header)
Fixed videos failing to load: the source container and codec now follow the archived file (mp4 vs webm) instead of always claiming video/mp4 + h264
Removed the stale s0.archive.party/.webm fallback url; the <video> source, its <source> or the download link is used instead
Added Cloudflare challenge detection with retries so challenge pages are never parsed or cached as content
8: Added a local media relay: when the plugin is loaded from a private address, thumbnails, channel avatars and video sources are fetched through that origin's /relay endpoint, so ISP content filters that block the s*.archive.party CDN (e.g. Xfinity Advanced Security / safebrowse.io) no longer break images or playback
The relay is only used when it is part of the plugin's own origin, so a plugin hosted normally keeps using PreserveTube's CDN directly
Thumbnails of older archives still pointed at the retired minio.lain.la mirror, which serves nothing any more; they now point at the same file on the host that serves their media
